With addictive gameplay, charming graphics, and a fantastic soundtrack, Peglin is a must-play for any fan of the genre
Great fun little game with lots of replayability and regular updates
A lot of fun, challenging, very replayable, overall a 10/10 game, better than most AAA's
I still really like it, and it is well worth the price
there is not enough meaningful content beyond that to justify the price tag
I now unfortunately regret that decision, as the game feels worse and worse for every update
I requested a refund and do not recommend this game
, I don't recommend people buy this game until they fix the actual ball and peg gameplay
I hate pegs, this game gives me a chance to show them how I feel.

I have loved peglin for a long time. I have also been frustrated with it almost every time there has been a change and new achieves. I mostly like to put a game to rest and not revisit it especially for insanely annoying rng reliant achieves.

So when Act 4 dropped and there were new achieves AGAIN I internally shuddered. And spent the first day of trying to get them swearing a lot.

But actually I really like peglin. And like the new level the more I play it. And honestly don't mind that it destroys me on some (many) runs. It makes it all the sweeter when I beat it.

So have fun with those orbs, you can beat the game with a number of builds. Just experiment.
And hopefully the rng gods will smile on you too.
The puns are terrorbly bad, but the game is ballin. They definitely also didn't drop the ball on artwork, vibe and general atmosphere. Did not disappoint.
an absolute banger. Simple to get into and just addicting enough to want to keep trying!
Easily my most anticipated game I've got cooking in early access, love everything it's got to offer.

I love the game. It is a simple but amazing game. My main issue is the slime boss. There is NO
reason for this boss to be so hard in the first chapter. It is a run killer. I'm starting to do seeds,
check if the boss is there, and if it is, just skip it and start another run, because it will kill my
run if I don't have a broken set of peglins by the end of the act or if I'm not full life to attempt
to kill it. It is frustrating and annoying. Remove the red orbs at least. This new "buff" is just
stupid - you increased its health, and added 4 or 5 red shitty orbs at the bottom of the level.
I'll come back to the game once this boss is either adjusted or removed, because having to
restart runs just to avoid one single boss is just incredibly stupid.
When things go wrong, it's RNG. When things go right, IT'S ALL YOU BABY PEGLIN POGLIN
The game is fantastic. One of the few roguelites I go back to after beating all the challenge levels. The randomness is a challenge but part of the charm.
Very fun, interesting, frustrating & great. Could use some more content, but worth the money. Also, cute Peglin:)

Great game that really nails the Peggle roots. Most downvotes at the time of this review are about lack of content, but that is what Early Access is about. Support the game and the dev if you enjoy Peggle and Rougelites :)
Fun at first, but poor balancing leaves you with a few options that are waaaay stronger than others, which makes runs without those options feel pointless.

The updates have been keeping the game fresh and I always look forward to playing again when I see something has been changed. This is definitely my kind of game! I absolutely see myself putting more hours into this joy of a game

Challenging rogue-like with a fun premise!

My main critique is that I think it's a bit too challenging to unlock the four unique characters, I've been playing for a while and have yet to unlock them all myself, but I think that's because the method of unlocking them forces you to learn how to use their character's core gameplay mechanic (e.g. building up a ton of block over the course of a battle gets you the Knight-styled character.) I wish the threshold for getting some of these characters was a bit easier, or maybe I'm just not having the best of luck with some of my runs.

I recommend this game for anyone who loves challenging games! Though like pretty much all rogue-likes there's a system to add difficulty to the game as you get better, so if you're just having fun watching the ball hit the pegs and the big number do big damage, Peglin's more than happy to keep you entertained there too

i cant in good conscience say this game is bad because its actually really fun and lovingly crafted but trying to beat every difficulty is also the worst thing i will EVER do to myself in my life. i dont think ive ever been more upset than while playing this game.

help.

A must buy for Peggle or Pachinko fans!

Peglin is a great Peggle style game with added RPG elements. You move along a branching over-world map with each branch decided on which route you choose by firing your Peglin Ball down the gutter of preset paths at the bottom of each board. You are awarded with gold each coin peg you shoot and various balls you can unlock/buy through progress. Any relics unlocked in the campaign are unlocked for the custom run mode as well allowing you to master your skills outside of the campaign. Each ball type has different stats and abilities allowing you to focus your Peglin build however you choose to defeat the enemies. With it's timeless pixel art and addictive puzzle/RPG game-play I'd say this game is a fine choice for those who wish to combine turn based RPG's and Peggle.

Every fun thing you can find in this game will be nerfed because for some reason the devs want the game to be so hard in normal mode even though they already claim that hard mode is impossible to beat. Let me have my casual fun in normal mode. Until the devs focus on letting the fun things remain in the game this game is just not worth anyone's time.

Honestly having more fun with this game than I thought I was going to. Its satisfying finding the right combination of relics and balls to get the effects you want. Sure, there's still RNG and you won't find the exact effects you wanted but its fun to improvise off what you have. 

And the dopamine rush you get from watching the ball bounce all over the place is fun too. 

Definitely a plus to being able to save and quit the game whenever so I want get a few quick rounds in.

This game is AWESOME! I have over 250 games in my library, and this game is already on my top 20 of most played games, soon to be on the top 10. And it's probably among the cheapest games I have. It combines the adictive fun and randomness of Peggle with a strategic gameplay that makes this game way deeper than the old Peggle games.

The game in its core is a roguelike, and you'll lose and start over a million times, but if you manage to beat the game (3 worlds with around 10-13 "levels" each), you can start your new round with a twist, that keeps adding. So after you beat the game the first time, maybe enemies will be a bit stronger. And if you manage to beat it that way, then you also start with less gold. And if you beat it like that, then next time you'll also have less special pegs on each level. And such, and such. This means you always have a new challenge to beat. After 80 hours, I'm at Cruciball level 9 and there seems to be at least 15. And you can also change the character at some point, which brings new game modes into the table.

Really, it's worth every penny. Try it, it won't dissapoint you.

Its SUCH A FUN GAME!! i love all the replay ability with you can have a completely different run no matter what or just try your hardest with getting certain strategies to work, i love it!! the art is so cute and the scenarios are funny sometimes. whenever an update comes out, i feel the immediate need to play all that i can. I will say the high cruciball stages are really difficult if you dont do cheese strats for a couple of them but it doesnt ruin it for me since its all optional. overall one of my favorite games to play!!

Peggle meets Slay the Spire.

A chill, strategic little deck builder where you play an adorable little goblin random encountering through 3 unique areas each with a boss waiting at the end. Each peg hit with your chosen orb racks up damage that you deal to enemies rushing you with every throw. Whether its poison, fortification, enhancing your pegs, or sheer chaos, there is a lot of ways to play such a minimalist game. However, there is an element of luck as you will find yourself fishing for certain random events, orbs, and upgrades to maximize your builds. This would be a problem if the game was any more difficult than mild; once you reach new game+8 it does. The music is also mild and unobtrusive but some tracks have the potential to be so ear wormy you will be still bobbing to them 50 hours in. My only complaint is that some of the achievements can be menacingly specific to reach, and you will need to be very lucky or laser focused for some of them.

A definite recommend as an unwind, brain off, after work game.

While content is on the lighter side for most well-known roguelikes, this game is still pretty good! it took me about 8 hours to beat for the first time and I am already starting to feel like I've just about gotten all I am going to get from this game in it's current state. Even saying that, it is still a well designed game and has a very charming energy. I am a sucker for pachinko machines and hitting a solid combo with the orbs you have meticulously picked out for your build each run is so so satisfying. I recommend this game if you can get it on a good sale, $15 or less is more than reasonable.

You ever just take a Boss Relic that doubles your damage, but makes it so that every 25 pegs you bump deals 3 damage to you?

Between that and the ball puns, I'm not sure what part of this game is my favorite.

I'm joking; it's the Punch sound effect.
lovely game to play once in a while, the bad thing is there isnt much content at the moment. :/

A classic "1000 hours, negative review" type situation here.

Balancing is pretty awful as you raise the ascensions. Which I think comes down to the core gameplay being so luck based. But while a run at ascension 20 in a game like Slay the Spire always feels winnable and you can often diagnose the issue with lost runs, this just feels like you're rolling a dice hoping to get good rolls, and if you don't you're just screwed. Also, they took the worst part of the Slay the Spire ascensions (adding a garbage card to your starting deck with limited utility and decided to do it twice in the ascensions???

It's fun enough, but it feels vapid compared to the games it's trying to live up to.

You know if you enjoy this type of game before you buy it. You also know that if for whatever reason you have a negative review of it you had plenty of evidence showing the game off on YouTube and could easily tell if you'd even like it in the first place.

Okay. I finally, after a hundred and fifty nine hours of playtime, got the mythic "sit back and do nothing" run. As I should have guessed, wasn't really all that fun. I really hope this convinces me to never reinstall the game again.

TO BE CLEAR: It's good (that's why I'm leaving this review as positive), and for those of you who enjoy gambling-related rougelikes, you can get a real fun time out of this. I think this game just doesn't mesh well with my addictive behavior. Once you get to the harder levels it's like hell, and through all the bull**** runs I kept coming back for more. Seriously, I don't know if the devs ever tested a playthrough beyond level 12, but it gets to be a serious slog that isn't even fun anymore.

Again, still a good game. Just be careful. If I'm lucky writing this will be the last I interact with it. It's destr orb ing my life!!!!

Nice little game with a lot of replayability.
Worth the full price, and it is still being updated with new things.

Making a turn-based RPG that combines the RNG in Peggle and roguelikes is evil and frustrating until in true rogue fashion you gain items and buffs that create multiballs that can hit several bombs at once for massive aoe damage before falling through the bottom to reappear at the top again to hit more pegs to do more damage on your turn.

You are certainly at the mercy of RNG twice as much as any other game, but the game is certainly made to accommodate just as insane items and buffs to compensate.
absolutely recommend the game, its a roguelike that has so much strategy and it's very fun when you get awesome combos

Review Version: 0.8.6 (Early Access)
If you liked peggle and like roguelikes, this game is a must-buy.

For everyone else, I'd say it's still worth the purchase. The game is fun and the developers are active, continuing to add new content and balancing the existing stuff. They've done quite a good job so far, in my opinion. The game's difficulty scaling is customizable to the point where you can make the game tough but fair.

TLDR: I've immensely enjoyed my time with Peglin, and I expect you would too.

a game all about "pegging" if you love "pegging" then this game is for YOU
nah fr though great game endless fun

this game drives me crazy, but I cant stop playing it.
if you like peggle, and beating your head against a wall, this game is for you
I've had an absolute blast playing this so far. It makes the brick breaking format fun and interesting again, and the roguelite elements keep it entertaining enough on replay.

As someone with over 1000 hours in Slay the Spire, I want to like this game. But the cruciball levels just feel unfair and not fun at times. It feels like you need some specific things in order to actually get past certain points, and there's times where the loss felt determined well before the fights themselves.
When you get a broken run going, it's great. Otherwise, hope you like dying. Maybe my experience is soured by climbing cruciball levels, but the higher levels didn't feel fair, and I didn't really feel like I was learning lessons in becoming a better player so much as I was falling behind until I got a run where the stars aligned and the game didn't feel like screwing me over.

I showed this game to a friend of mine once, and his comment was "Hmm, there seems to be a bit of gameplay in that collection of puns".
The idea of turning a pachinko game into a roguelike is very unique, and the various orbs and relics are extremely interesting. I love the pixelart graphics, not only because they're pretty cute and very well done, but also because it makes the game perform really good on my low-end pc. I also find it pretty neat how, instead of making you stronger, progressing through the game actually makes you gradually weaker, as it really impacts the strategies that you have to choose.
Overall, I'm in love with this game, looking forward to the next updates

Be careful with this game. I play a lot of rogue-likes with my wife and we picked up this one after finishing slay the spire. We are almost 200 hours deep into Peglin and she refuses any attempt to stop playing it. My only hope is that the developers will sunset the project. Please send help.

Edit: It has been an additional 150 hours. I have lost hope in help ever arriving. Now I play Peglin.

Peglin is a great little roguelite deckbuilder, RNG elements, mechanics are easy enough to understand and work around, some really fun combos, without a steep learning curve. Great casual game to play.

Only thing I'd prefer is a little QOL with the boon selection at the start of higher cruciballs (Prestige/challenge modes), otherwise you're just going back to new game to refresh all the time.

Great game overall, would recommend.

Game isn't great. Been out forever, but still feels incomplete. Levels and progression are almost all the same. Tons of items, but very few of them good, and rarely ever contribute to a viable build, leaving you with a slow, boring bleed to the end - sometimes of the game; usually of your life. Been trying for half of my playtime for a single achievement, and can't get the items needed to accomplish it. Just level after level of frustrating RNG. 

Skip.
Play Peglin because my girlfriend likes it. She put all these hours on it LOL. Nearly 100% too

Peggle, Round Guard, and Peglin, all so good.

This one has you hitting pegs to acrue gold & affect damage and not all areas you go to have a fight.
You make choices between beneficial relics and stones used, with effects and upgrades.

Decently explained if I recall and right up there with Peggle and Round Guard as best in genre!

As it stands, worth it IMHO.

This game is so fun and satisfying! It's one I love to come back to when I just want to turn my brain off for half an hour. The devs are active and continue to add great updates to the game. I wish it had additional locations/monsters, and that the runs were a bit longer, but it is still a lovely little game worth the full price. It is a rougelike, rng and luck are core mechanics, so if you don't like those things, this game is probably not for you.

This was a tough one for me. I really wanted to give it a positive review... The Idea is great and the game play shows a lot of promise. The downside is the frustration around several encounter types and the navigation of the board. I would have liked a choice for navigation where I could just pick the route I want to go rather than having to shoot a ball and hope I get to go the right way. At least a choice where If I pick the path I don't get any extra money or healing provided by the relics and orbs. The encounters with the Wall (second stage boss) which even if you played perfectly up till that point is too big of a hurdle as about I lose about 80 percent of the time. I find many play styles would just fail outright at it. The other encounter with the long line of exploding goblins always ends my run. Doesn't seem to matter what orbs or relics I have they win. They do 40 damage a hit and have more health combined that most bosses. I'm at the point where I just close the game and start over at this encounter. With these issues which pop up way to often I just cant' recommend it.

The devs aren't trying to make a "fun" game.

This game always gets updated ruining some fun thing that's found every time without fail. All the devs want is a hard game with "balance" that isn't a fun balance but just hard and unnecessary. There is literally a level in the second area that will without fail end your run if you don't have a certain type of orb, and even then it still can easily kill you! This game has and has had so much potential! But this game is just... not going in the right direction.

I do not recommend this game.

So poorly balanced with crucible I do not recommend buying.

Dev has done nothing but nerf the good things to no longer be fun and buff enemies and flood boss fights with minions that makes most builds unviable in later crucible levels. You just end up exiting and starting again till you get the exact items you need for a very small selection of boring builds.

Game just isn't fun once you've played for a bit.
an absolutely incredible concept. was engaged at every second trying to think of new builds and orb combos. I truly hope this game gets more levels and characters to play
i love peggle and i love when the numbers get big literally whats not to like
As a local goblin, I highly recommend peglin for getting the level 1 goblin experience.

Fun music and art style, but the physics of the ball and pegs feel very irregular, and the first few levels are probably harder than the devs meant them to be due to so few pegs on the board. All to often you get to hit one peg and then the ball flies down a Hole for minimal damage

Peglin's gameplay is extremely unique, fun and satsifying but it doesn't really reach its full potential.

If you play the free demo, you've practically played the entire game. Every run feels extremely samey, and after beating the measly 3 worlds that are included in this game (Which are identical every time) you have practically no reason to pick the game up again. The only progression that can be found are the few unlockable characters but they all feel almost the exact same and felt very underwhelming to unlock. This game has a lot of potential, but I don't see it being worth the €16 I've spent on it. I had faith, buying it in early access- however the game is now close to completion and it's just as shallow as it was when I first got it. The devs are playing it very safe and refuse to add anything that would shake up this stale gameplay loop, so I suggest you spend your money elsewhere.
Fun and addictive little rogue-like heavily inspired by Peggle from back in the day. Very nostalgic for me whilst still feeling super modern in it's design. Love it.
